critical_rubrics: Must state both $\delta_\eta\phi$ and its Hermitian conjugate with the correct coefficient and spinor contraction; must also note that the total action variation reduces to a spacetime total derivative (hence invariance) under the stated assumptions.

step_results.description: Introduce the most general Lorentz-covariant linear ansatz for the missing scalar variation, $�\delta_{\eta}\phi=a\,\eta^{\alpha}\xi_{\alpha}$, and its Hermitian conjugate $(\delta_{\eta}\phi)^{\dagger}=a^{*}\,\bar{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}\bar{\xi}^{\dot{\alpha}}$, with an undetermined constant $a$; this uses only that $�\phi$ is complex scalar, $�\eta$ and $�\xi$ are Weyl spinors, and $�\eta$ is spacetime independent.
step_results.reasoning: Since $\delta_\eta\phi$ must transform as a Lorentz scalar, the spinor indices of the two left-handed Weyl spinors $\eta^\alpha$ and $\xi_\alpha$ must be contracted. Under the assumed linearity in the SUSY parameter and the fields, the only available Lorentz-scalar contraction is $\eta^\alpha\xi_\alpha$, up to an overall complex coefficient $a$. Because $\eta$ is spacetime independent, no derivative acting on $\eta$ is introduced. Taking the Hermitian conjugate maps undotted spinors to dotted spinors and gives the scalar contraction $\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha}$ multiplied by $a^*$.
step_results.result:
Introduce an undetermined complex constant $a$ and write the most general Lorentz-covariant linear scalar variation as
$$
\delta_\eta \phi = a\,\eta^\alpha \xi_\alpha \equiv a\,\eta\xi .
$$
Its Hermitian conjugate is therefore
$$
(\delta_\eta\phi)^\dagger = a^*\,(\eta^\alpha\xi_\alpha)^\dagger
= a^*\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha}
\equiv a^*\,\bar\eta\bar\xi .
$$
This is the most general form at this stage because $\phi$ is a complex Lorentz scalar, $\eta$ and $\xi$ are Weyl spinors, the variation is assumed linear in the fields and in the constant SUSY parameter, and $\eta$ is spacetime independent; no invariance condition has yet been used to fix $a$.

step_results.description: Vary the scalar kinetic term $|\partial\phi|^{2}=\partial_{\mu}\bar{\phi}\,\partial^{\mu}\phi$ using the ansatz from Step 1, integrate by parts in the action, and isolate the terms proportional to $\eta\,\partial\xi\,\partial\bar{\phi}$ and $\bar{\eta}\,\partial\bar{\xi}\,\partial\phi$ that must cancel against corresponding pieces from the fermion kinetic variation.
step_results.reasoning: The scalar kinetic term depends only on derivatives of $\phi$ and $\bar\phi$, so its variation is obtained by the product rule. Since $\eta$ and $\bar\eta$ are constant infinitesimal parameters, derivatives act only on $\xi$ and $\bar\xi$ after inserting the Step 1 ansatz. In the action, integration by parts permits dropping total derivatives and rewriting the variation either in terms of $\delta\phi\,\Box\bar\phi$ and $\delta\bar\phi\,\Box\phi$, or equivalently in the first-derivative form. The latter directly displays the two structures relevant for cancellation with the derivative-dependent pieces of the fermion kinetic variation: one proportional to $\eta\,\partial\xi\,\partial\bar\phi$ with coefficient $a$, and its conjugate proportional to $\bar\eta\,\partial\bar\xi\,\partial\phi$ with coefficient $a^*$.
step_results.result:
Using
$$
\delta_\eta\phi=a\,\eta^\alpha\xi_\alpha,\qquad \delta_\eta\bar\phi=a^*\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha},
$$
and $\partial_\mu\eta=\partial_\mu\bar\eta=0$, the scalar kinetic term varies as
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_{\phi}
=\delta_\eta\left(\partial_\mu\bar\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi\right)
=\partial_\mu(\delta_\eta\bar\phi)\,\partial^\mu\phi
+\partial_\mu\bar\phi\,\partial^\mu(\delta_\eta\phi).
$$
Substituting the ansatz gives
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_{\phi}
=a^*\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\,\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha}\,\partial^\mu\phi
+a\,\partial_\mu\bar\phi\,\eta^\alpha\partial^\mu\xi_\alpha.
$$
Equivalently, in the action one may first integrate by parts:
$$
\delta_\eta S_\phi
=\int d^4x\left[\partial_\mu(\delta\bar\phi)\partial^\mu\phi+\partial_\mu\bar\phi\partial^\mu(\delta\phi)\right]
=-\int d^4x\left[\delta\bar\phi\,\Box\phi+(\Box\bar\phi)\delta\phi\right],
$$
up to a surface term. Inserting the ansatz and integrating by parts back onto the fermions yields the same non-boundary contribution
$$
\delta_\eta S_\phi
=\int d^4x\left[
a\,\eta^\alpha(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)\partial^\mu\bar\phi
+a^*\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}(\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha})\partial^\mu\phi
\right].
$$
Thus the isolated terms that must cancel the corresponding fermion-kinetic variation are
$$
\boxed{a\,\eta^\alpha(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)\partial^\mu\bar\phi}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\boxed{a^*\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}(\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha})\partial^\mu\phi}.
$$

step_results.reasoning: Start from the product variation of $i\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\xi$. The $\partial\bar\phi$ term comes directly from $\delta\bar\xi$ and has coefficient $i(-i\sqrt2)=+\sqrt2$. The $\partial\phi$ term comes from the derivative acting on the derivative part of $\delta\xi$, with coefficient $i(i\sqrt2)=-\sqrt2$ and a second derivative $\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\phi$; integrating by parts transfers one derivative onto $\bar\xi$, changing the sign to $+\sqrt2$. In each resulting expression, only the symmetric part of the sigma-matrix product contributes nontrivially after discarding total derivatives, because the antisymmetric part contracted with two spacetime derivatives can be written as a surface term. The symmetric sigma products reduce to $\eta^{\mu\nu}$ times Kronecker deltas, yielding exactly the same two structures isolated in Step 2, with coefficients $\sqrt2$ and $\sqrt2$.
step_results.result:
The fermion kinetic variation is
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi
=i\,\delta\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha}\bar\sigma^{\mu\dot\alpha\alpha}\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha
+i\,\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha}\bar\sigma^{\mu\dot\alpha\alpha}\partial_\mu(\delta\xi_\alpha).
$$
Keeping only the derivative-of-$\phi$ and derivative-of-$\bar\phi$ pieces gives
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi\big|_{\partial\phi}
=\sqrt2\,\eta^\beta\sigma^\nu_{\beta\dot\alpha}\bar\sigma^{\mu\dot\alpha\alpha}
(\partial_\nu\bar\phi)(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)
-\sqrt2\,\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha}\bar\sigma^{\mu\dot\alpha\alpha}\sigma^\nu_{\alpha\dot\beta}\bar\eta^{\dot\beta}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\phi .
$$
For the second term, integrate by parts in the action:
$$
\int d^4x\,[-\sqrt2\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha}\bar\sigma^{\mu\dot\alpha\alpha}\sigma^\nu_{\alpha\dot\beta}\bar\eta^{\dot\beta}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\phi]
=\int d^4x\,\sqrt2(\partial_\mu\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha})\bar\sigma^{\mu\dot\alpha\alpha}\sigma^\nu_{\alpha\dot\beta}\bar\eta^{\dot\beta}\partial_\nu\phi,
$$
up to a surface term. In both terms the antisymmetric part in $\mu,\nu$ is a total derivative, so using
$$
\bar\sigma^{\mu\dot\alpha\alpha}\sigma^\nu_{\alpha\dot\beta}
+\bar\sigma^{\nu\dot\alpha\alpha}\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}
=2\eta^{\mu\nu}\delta^{\dot\alpha}{}_{\dot\beta}
$$
and the analogous $\sigma\bar\sigma$ identity, the non-boundary derivative contribution becomes
$$
\boxed{\delta_\eta S_\xi\big|_{\partial\phi}
=\int d^4x\left[
\sqrt2\,\eta^\alpha(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)\partial^\mu\bar\phi
+\sqrt2\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}(\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha})\partial^\mu\phi
\right]}.
$$
Equivalently, modulo total derivatives,
$$
\boxed{\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi\big|_{\partial\phi}
\doteq
\sqrt2\,\eta^\alpha(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)\partial^\mu\bar\phi
+\sqrt2\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}(\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha})\partial^\mu\phi}.
$$

step_results.description: Equate the coefficients of the independent derivative structures obtained in Steps 2 and 3 to determine the constant $a$, ensuring that Grassmann signs from moving $�\eta$ through $�\xi$ and $�\bar{\xi}$ are treated consistently.
step_results.reasoning: From Step 2, the scalar kinetic variation contributes coefficients $a$ and $a^*$ multiplying the two independent derivative structures. From Step 3, the fermion kinetic variation contributes $+\sqrt2$ to each corresponding structure, after integration by parts and discarding total derivatives. Since these derivative structures are independent and cannot cancel against the auxiliary-field variation, invariance of the action requires the sum of the scalar and fermion coefficients to vanish separately. Hence $a+\sqrt2=0$ and $a^*+\sqrt2=0$, giving $a=-\sqrt2$. Care must be taken not to introduce an additional erroneous sign when moving $\eta$ or $\bar\eta$ through $\xi$ or $\bar\xi$: the final matching is done only after all expressions have been put into the same canonical Grassmann ordering and spinor-index convention.
step_results.result:
The derivative-dependent part of the total variation of the action is, up to surface terms,
$$
\delta_\eta S\big|_{\partial\phi}
=\int d^4x\,\Big[(a+\sqrt2)\,\eta^\alpha(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)\partial^\mu\bar\phi
+(a^*+\sqrt2)\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}(\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha})\partial^\mu\phi\Big].
$$
The two structures
$$
\eta^\alpha(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)\partial^\mu\bar\phi,
\qquad
\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}(\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha})\partial^\mu\phi
$$
are independent, so their coefficients must vanish separately:
$$
a+\sqrt2=0,
\qquad
a^*+\sqrt2=0.
$$
Therefore
$$
\boxed{a=-\sqrt2},
\qquad
\boxed{a^*=-\sqrt2}.
$$
Thus the scalar variation fixed by cancellation of the derivative terms is
$$
\boxed{\delta_\eta\phi=-\sqrt2\,\eta^\alpha\xi_\alpha}
$$
and its Hermitian conjugate is
$$
\boxed{(\delta_\eta\phi)^\dagger=-\sqrt2\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha}}.
$$
The Grassmann signs are consistent because all terms have been expressed with the fermionic parameter placed in the same canonical position. In particular, when rewriting dotted contractions such as $(\partial_\mu\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha})\bar\eta^{\dot\alpha}$ as $\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}(\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha})$, the minus sign from exchanging two Grassmann-odd quantities is compensated by the antisymmetry of the spinor metric used to raise and lower dotted indices.

step_results.description: Vary the auxiliary-field term $-|F|^{2}=-\bar{F}F$ using the given $�\delta_{\eta}F$ and $�\delta_{\eta}\bar{F}$, and combine it with the $F$-dependent part of the fermion kinetic variation from Step 3 to verify that these terms cancel for the same value of $a$ found in Step 4.
step_results.reasoning: The auxiliary term only depends on $F$ and $\bar F$, so its variation is directly $-(\delta\bar F)F-\bar F\delta F$. Substituting the given SUSY variations gives two terms: one proportional to $F\partial\bar\xi\bar\sigma\eta$ and one proportional to $\bar F\bar\eta\bar\sigma\partial\xi$. The fermion kinetic term contains corresponding $F$-dependent pieces because $\delta\xi$ has a $\sqrt2\eta F$ term and $\delta\bar\xi$ has a $\sqrt2\bar\eta\bar F$ term. The $\bar F$ term cancels locally against the second auxiliary variation. The $F$ term first appears as $\bar\xi\bar\sigma\eta\partial F$ and cancels the first auxiliary variation after integrating by parts in the action. Since $\eta$ is spacetime independent and $F$ is bosonic, no extra sign arises in the integration by parts beyond the usual minus sign. The cancellation is independent of the scalar-variation coefficient $a$, so it remains valid for the Step 4 value $a=-\sqrt2$.
step_results.result:
The auxiliary-field contribution is
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_F=\delta_\eta(-\bar F F)=-(\delta_\eta\bar F)F-\bar F(\delta_\eta F).
$$
Using
$$
\delta_\eta F=i\sqrt2\,\bar\eta\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\xi,
\qquad
\delta_\eta\bar F=-i\sqrt2\,\partial_\mu\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta,
$$
one obtains
$$
\boxed{\delta_\eta\mathcal L_F
= i\sqrt2\,F\,\partial_\mu\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta
-i\sqrt2\,\bar F\,\bar\eta\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\xi.}
$$
Now isolate the $F$-dependent part of the fermion kinetic variation
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi=i\delta\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\xi+i\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu(\delta\xi).
$$
From
$$
\delta\bar\xi\big|_{\bar F}=\sqrt2\bar\eta\bar F,
\qquad
\delta\xi\big|_F=\sqrt2\eta F,
$$
we get
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi\big|_F
=i\sqrt2\,\bar F\,\bar\eta\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\xi
+i\sqrt2\,\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta\,\partial_\mu F.
$$
In the action, integrate the second term by parts, with $\eta$ constant:
$$
\int d^4x\,i\sqrt2\,\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta\,\partial_\mu F
\doteq
-\int d^4x\,i\sqrt2\,F\,\partial_\mu\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta,
$$
where $\doteq$ denotes equality up to a total derivative. Hence
$$
\boxed{\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi\big|_F
\doteq
 i\sqrt2\,\bar F\,\bar\eta\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\xi
-i\sqrt2\,F\,\partial_\mu\bar\xi\bar\sigma^\mu\eta.}
$$
Adding this to $\delta_\eta\mathcal L_F$ gives
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_F+\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi\big|_F\doteq 0.
$$
Thus the $F$-dependent terms cancel off shell, modulo a total derivative. This cancellation does not introduce any new condition on $a$; it is therefore consistent with the value already fixed in Step 4, namely
$$
a=a^*=-\sqrt2.
$$

step_results.description: State the resulting $�\delta_{\eta}\phi$ and $(\delta_{\eta}\phi)^{\dagger}$, and note that the full variation of the action is a spacetime total derivative under the assumptions used above.
step_results.reasoning: From the prior steps, the scalar variation was fixed by cancellation of the derivative terms in the variation of the action. The unique Lorentz-covariant choice consistent with invariance is $\delta_\eta\phi=a\,\eta\xi$ with $a=-\sqrt2$, hence $\delta_\eta\phi=-\sqrt2\,\eta\xi$. Taking the Hermitian conjugate gives $(\delta_\eta\phi)^\dagger=-\sqrt2\,\bar\eta\bar\xi$. With these transformations, together with the given variations of $\xi$ and $F$, all non-boundary terms cancel pairwise, so the remaining variation of the Lagrangian is a spacetime total derivative.
step_results.result: $$\delta_\eta\phi=-\sqrt{2}\,\eta^\alpha\xi_\alpha,\qquad (\delta_\eta\phi)^\dagger=-\sqrt{2}\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha}. $$ Under the assumptions used above (constant SUSY parameter $\eta$, integrations by parts, and the standard two-component spinor identities), the full variation of the action is a spacetime total derivative, so the action is invariant.

# Physics Problem Notebook

: Topic:
SUSY-Symmetry

Problem:
Consider the theory
\begin{equation}
\mathcal{L}=i\bar{\xi}\bar{\sigma}^{\mu}\partial_{\mu}\xi+|\partial\phi|^{2}-|F|^{2}
\end{equation}
where $\xi$ is a 2-component Weyl spinor while $\phi$ and $F$ are
complex scalar fields. Suppose you want to make the following infinitesimal
transformation a symmetry of this theory:
\begin{equation}
\delta_{\eta}\xi_{\alpha}=i\sqrt{2}\sigma_{\alpha\dot{\alpha}}^{\mu}\bar{\eta}^{\dot{\alpha}}\partial_{\mu}\phi+\sqrt{2}\eta_{\alpha}F
\end{equation}
\begin{align*}
\delta_{\eta}\bar{\xi}_{\dot{\beta}} & = [i\sqrt{2}\sigma_{\beta\dot{\alpha}}^{\mu}\bar{\eta}^{\dot{\alpha}}\partial_{\mu}\phi+\sqrt{2}\eta_{\beta}F]^{\dagger}\\
 & = -i\sqrt{2}(\bar{\eta}^{\dot{\alpha}}\sigma_{\dot{\alpha}\beta}^{\mu*})^{*}\partial_{\mu}\bar{\phi}+\sqrt{2}\bar{\eta}_{\dot{\beta}}\bar{F}\\
 & = -i\sqrt{2}\eta^{\alpha}\sigma_{\alpha\dot{\beta}}^{\mu}\partial_{\mu}\bar{\phi}+\sqrt{2}\bar{\eta}_{\dot{\beta}}\bar{F}\numberthis
\end{align*}
\begin{equation}
\delta_{\eta}F=i\sqrt{2}\bar{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}\bar{\sigma}^{\mu\dot{\alpha}\alpha}\partial_{\mu}\xi_{\alpha}=i\sqrt{2}\bar{\eta}\bar{\sigma}^{\mu}\partial_{\mu}\xi
\end{equation}
\begin{align*}
\delta_{\eta}\bar{F} & = -i\sqrt{2}(\bar{\eta}\bar{\sigma}^{\mu}\partial_{\mu}\xi)^{\dagger}\\
 & = -i\sqrt{2}(\partial_{\mu}\xi)^{\dagger}(\bar{\sigma}^{\mu})^{\dagger}(\bar{\eta})^{\dagger}\\
 & = -i\sqrt{2}\partial_{\mu}\bar{\xi}\bar{\sigma}^{\mu}\eta\numberthis
\end{align*}
along with $\delta_{\eta}\phi$ and $\left(\delta_{\eta}\phi\right)^{\dagger}$
where $\eta$ is a spacetime-independent infinitesimal fermionic parameter
inducing the transformation. Find the transformation rule $\delta_{\eta}\phi$
and $\left(\delta_{\eta}\phi\right)^{\dagger}$ for the action associated
with $\mathcal{L}$ to remain invariant.

Domain:
HET


## Step 1: Introduce the most general Lorentz-covariant linear ansatz for the missing scalar variation, $�\delta_{\eta}\phi=a\,\eta^{\alpha}\xi_{\alpha}$, and its Hermitian conjugate $(\delta_{\eta}\phi)^{\dagger}=a^{*}\,\bar{\eta}_{\dot{\alpha}}\bar{\xi}^{\dot{\alpha}}$, with an undetermined constant $a$; this uses only that $�\phi$ is complex scalar, $�\eta$ and $�\xi$ are Weyl spinors, and $�\eta$ is spacetime independent.

**Result:** Introduce an undetermined complex constant $a$ and write the most general Lorentz-covariant linear scalar variation as
$$
\delta_\eta \phi = a\,\eta^\alpha \xi_\alpha \equiv a\,\eta\xi .
$$
Its Hermitian conjugate is therefore
$$
(\delta_\eta\phi)^\dagger = a^*\,(\eta^\alpha\xi_\alpha)^\dagger
= a^*\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha}
\equiv a^*\,\bar\eta\bar\xi .
$$
This is the most general form at this stage because $\phi$ is a complex Lorentz scalar, $\eta$ and $\xi$ are Weyl spinors, the variation is assumed linear in the fields and in the constant SUSY parameter, and $\eta$ is spacetime independent; no invariance condition has yet been used to fix $a$.


## Step 2: Vary the scalar kinetic term $|\partial\phi|^{2}=\partial_{\mu}\bar{\phi}\,\partial^{\mu}\phi$ using the ansatz from Step 1, integrate by parts in the action, and isolate the terms proportional to $\eta\,\partial\xi\,\partial\bar{\phi}$ and $\bar{\eta}\,\partial\bar{\xi}\,\partial\phi$ that must cancel against corresponding pieces from the fermion kinetic variation.

**Result:** Using
$$
\delta_\eta\phi=a\,\eta^\alpha\xi_\alpha,\qquad \delta_\eta\bar\phi=a^*\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha},
$$
and $\partial_\mu\eta=\partial_\mu\bar\eta=0$, the scalar kinetic term varies as
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_{\phi}
=\delta_\eta\left(\partial_\mu\bar\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi\right)
=\partial_\mu(\delta_\eta\bar\phi)\,\partial^\mu\phi
+\partial_\mu\bar\phi\,\partial^\mu(\delta_\eta\phi).
$$
Substituting the ansatz gives
$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_{\phi}
=a^*\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}\,\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha}\,\partial^\mu\phi
+a\,\partial_\mu\bar\phi\,\eta^\alpha\partial^\mu\xi_\alpha.
$$
Equivalently, in the action one may first integrate by parts:
$$
\delta_\eta S_\phi

=-\int d^4x\left[\delta\bar\phi\,\Box\phi+(\Box\bar\phi)\delta\phi\right],

$$

a\,\eta^\alpha(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)\partial^\mu\bar\phi

\right].
$$
Thus the isolated terms that must cancel the corresponding fermion-kinetic variation are
$$
\boxed{a\,\eta^\alpha(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)\partial^\mu\bar\phi}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\boxed{a^*\,\bar\eta_{\dot\alpha}(\partial_\mu\bar\xi^{\dot\alpha})\partial^\mu\phi}.
$$


## Step 3: Vary the fermion kinetic term $i\bar{\xi}\bar{\sigma}^{\mu}\partial_{\mu}\xi$ using the given $�\delta_{\eta}\xi_{\alpha}$ and $�\delta_{\eta}\bar{\xi}_{\dot{\beta}}$, then use the two-component identity $\bar{\sigma}^{\mu\dot{\alpha}\alpha}\sigma^{\nu}_{\alpha\dot{\beta}}+\bar{\sigma}^{\nu\dot{\alpha}\alpha}\sigma^{\mu}_{\alpha\dot{\beta}}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}\delta^{\dot{\alpha}}{}_{\dot{\beta}}$ and discard total derivatives to express its derivative-of-$\phi$ contribution in the same structures isolated in Step 2.

$$
\delta_\eta\mathcal L_\xi
=i\,\delta\bar\xi_{\dot\alpha}\bar\sigma^{\mu\dot\alpha\alpha}\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha

## Step 4: Equate the coefficients of the independent derivative structures obtained in Steps 2 and 3 to determine the constant $a$, ensuring that Grassmann signs from moving $�\eta$ through $�\xi$ and $�\bar{\xi}$ are treated consistently.

**Result:** The derivative-dependent part of the total variation of the action is, up to surface terms,
$$
\delta_\eta S\big|_{\partial\phi}
=\int d^4x\,\Big[(a+\sqrt2)\,\eta^\alpha(\partial_\mu\xi_\alpha)\partial^\mu\bar\phi

The two structures

## Step 5: Vary the auxiliary-field term $-|F|^{2}=-\bar{F}F$ using the given $�\delta_{\eta}F$ and $�\delta_{\eta}\bar{F}$, and combine it with the $F$-dependent part of the fermion kinetic variation from Step 3 to verify that these terms cancel for the same value of $a$ found in Step 4.
